items.question: What is an annotation in Java?
items.answer:
Answer: An annotation is additional information written along with Java source code to communicate information about a program element. In Java, an annotation begins with the @ symbol. For example:

```java
@Override
```

An annotation is not a normal executable statement. It provides additional information that can be used by the compiler, JVM-related mechanisms, development tools, or other programmers working with the code.

items.question: What is the basic meaning of notation?
items.answer: Answer: Notation means communicating information to someone in written form. For example, a written note can communicate an instruction or message even when the person who wrote it is not physically present. The same basic idea can be related to programming annotations: information is written along with the program so that the intended information is available to the relevant person or software component.

What is constructor chaining in Java?
Why is constructor chaining useful?
Which keyword is used for constructor chaining within the same class?
items.answer:
Answer: The this keyword is used for constructor chaining within the same class. Examples:

```java
this();
```

calls the zero-parameter constructor.

```java
this(brand);
```

calls a constructor with one parameter.

```java
this(brand, model, price);
```

calls a constructor with three parameters.

What is the super keyword in Java?
items.answer: Answer: The super keyword is used in a child class to refer specifically to members of its immediate parent class. It can be used when access to the parent implementation or parent member is required. For example: super.a refers to the parent-class variable a.
